title: Independent parallel VIB lanes with self-managed verified checkpoints
summary: Extend VIB prospectively from one global active Worker to independent owner-authorized issue lanes that recover state, develop, validate and deliver without cross-thread dependencies. Preserve Solo mode, stable issue versions, exact evidence, dedicated branch installation, owner authority and independent product scope.
benefits: Independent ChatGPT or compatible agent sessions do not require another thread to coordinate or validate routine work.
Persistent issue-level state and conflict-safe version allocation preserve progress and reduce redundant coordination.
Preserve existing Solo installations and qualify Parallel mode without delaying the current release.
risks: Concurrent claims or stale writes may duplicate checkpoint assignments or lose state unless atomic non-force updates and idempotent retry are verified.
Overlapping changes may invalidate evidence; lane isolation cannot eliminate real code dependencies.
Self-review is not independent review, and Standard VIB does not enforce GitHub merges.
Unbounded expansion could delay releases or duplicate other ecosystem products; qualify five lanes and measure actual completion benefit.

evidence.claim: Existing source defines one active Worker; new Parallel mode must prospectively supersede only the global active slot restriction.
All six ecosystem laws remain in force; no mandatory coordinator or dependencies.
Original single-writer idea is preserved as historical context and Solo mode.

decision.reason: Owner approved the architecture direction; timestamp records public decision issue creation, not exact chat approval time. See https://github.com/vixttha/Version-Issues-Hub/issues/53. No implementation, integration or release acceptance is asserted.
